baseline.windows: Checked-out Rufus 4.15.2404 source, not latest upstream

activity: CP78 prepares the useful x86-64 GitHub release with original Rufus catalog reuse, accepted Linux-specific English fallback, Debian/Fedora native package qualification and manual AUR source submission files. Retained media evidence is reconciled; non-x64 To Go, additional hosts and unavailable physical hardware remain explicit qualification gaps. Full Windows parity is not claimed.
meaning: Rows are acceptance work packages, not independent checkpoints, equal effort units or a percentage estimate. open_work retains all unresolved rows, including explicitly deferred ones; progress.open_counts counts active rows only. Closed groups have explicit extension rows; coverage mapping is a disposition audit, not fresh runtime verification.
change_rule: A new parity item needs a concrete Windows release-dispatch/eligibility reference, native counter-evidence and de-duplication against this register. Record it in the owning batch. Do not reopen a closed group from dormant enums, broad combinations or optional per-version/per-device testing.

open_work.title: Native user-facing translation coverage

native.anchor: Translation coverage remains an open parity item

open_work.finding: The original 38-language selector and reused messages work. Native-only user-facing diagnostics, filters and unmatched templates still fall back to English.
open_work.acceptance: Freeze an inventory of reachable native user-facing strings, reuse original message IDs where equivalent and supply reviewed native translations for the declared languages. Record original catalog inheritance/fallback separately. Check placeholders, plural forms, filters, RTL and live cached dialogs. Do not translate technical trace logs merely because Windows also logs them in English.
open_work.scheduling_decision: 2026-10-24 user: reuse Rufus translations and document Linux-specific English fallback for the first useful release. Full native translations remain a follow-up; earlier full-translation release scheduling is superseded.
open_work.release_acceptance: Inventory literal native UI strings, bind equivalent original catalog messages safely, preserve placeholders and English fallback, and qualify live language/RTL/dialog behavior. Document catalog inheritance and unmatched native text. Do not claim full native translation coverage.

open_work.title: Microsoft Dev Drive exclusion
open_work.finding: Sandbox/antivirus exclusions exist; the Windows Dev Drive volume-state exclusion has no native metadata probe.
open_work.acceptance: Recognize the actual on-disk Dev Drive state using a bounded read-only native provider and exclude it under the original virtual-drive rule. Prove positive, negative and unavailable/corrupt-metadata behavior. Do not guess from a volume label.
open_work.dependency_note: For future resumption, a bounded read-only ReFS/Dev Drive metadata provider is required independently of the deferred formatter I15. Actual Dev Drive recognition is user-deferred; existing native protections remain and do not establish Dev Drive membership. Do not infer state from a label.
open_work.scheduling_decision: 2026-10-24 user after provider audit: "let's just skip this Dev Drive entirely too". Exclude actual Dev Drive detection from this release; no blanket ReFS virtual-disk refusal or label-based substitute. Existing native protections remain.

open_work.title: UDF 2.50 and 2.60 metadata partitions
open_work.finding: The integrated udftools 2.3 path implements revisions 1.02, 1.50, 2.00 and 2.01; metadata-partition revisions are absent.
open_work.acceptance: Deliver a native formatter/provider for actual 2.50 and 2.60 metadata-partition media, independent descriptor/readback verification, revision selection and original eligible layouts. Include full/quick, cancel, label and completion semantics; never silently substitute a lower revision. Audit provider licensing/maintenance and concrete on-disk compatibility first.
open_work.scheduling_decision: 2026-10-24 user: defer B6, document the UDF 2.50/2.60 gap and keep existing UDF support; prioritize a useful release. This remains an unimplemented full-parity gap.

open_work.title: Native ReFS formatting provider

native.anchor: ReFS formatting excluded from the first release

open_work.finding: No native ReFS formatting case/provider is integrated. Existing provider investigation did not identify an integrated formatter.
open_work.acceptance: Deliver a licensed native formatter with independent metadata/readback checks and matching applicable fixed-media, capacity and 4/64-KiB cluster eligibility. Establish actual Windows provider revision/capacity support; add MBR/GPT/SFD and normal helper/quick/full/cancel/label behavior where offered. An unavailable provider remains an open feature, not a completed limitation.
open_work.scheduling_decision: 2026-10-24 user response "remove just ReFS": exclude the ReFS formatter from first-release requirements, retain it as an unimplemented full-parity gap. Do not defer Dev Drive protection, applicable indexing hints, full translations or Q01–Q04.

open_work.title: UDF/ReFS file indexing hint

native.anchor: Windows also attempts the indexing hint

open_work.finding: NTFS has the real root indexing flag. CP77 preserves the saved supported-UDF choice and reports an optional unsupported-provider diagnostic when disabling indexing is requested. The actual Windows UDF attribute is not implemented on disk; Windows driver acceptance remains unverified.
open_work.acceptance: Implement each provider-supported Windows on-disk hint and inspect it independently, or prove the original provider does not support it and reproduce its optional-failure diagnostic/eligibility. Desktop search preferences alone are not an equivalent. Preserve saved Alt+Q state across filesystem changes.
open_work.scheduling_note: Keep the hint on existing UDF revisions active for this release. Newer-UDF and ReFS hints follow deferred I14/I15 providers; this does not defer the whole adaptation.
open_work.release_acceptance: Preserve/freeze Alt+Q on supported UDF jobs; retain NTFS-only compression and canonical admission; after successful UDF formatting report the unavailable optional Windows attribute only when disabling indexing was requested. Preserve file creation, sync, cleanup and joined READY. Disclose that the actual UDF attribute is not written and Windows acceptance is unverified.
open_work.native_difference: Linux UDF has no corresponding attribute-write interface or specified equivalent mapping. Match original Rufus best-effort failure semantics with a truthful diagnostic; no guessed UDF bit, desktop-indexer substitution or claim that Windows rejects it. Actual on-disk metadata parity remains unresolved in this row; the release policy is qualified.

open_work.finding: Most media behavior already has component, native guest/readback and representative firmware evidence; additional sources/geometry above need one final reconciliation.
open_work.acceptance: Produce one evidence manifest for the 10 boot choices, the 8 actually selectable filesystems, MBR/GPT/SFD, BIOS/UEFI, original expert/advanced flags and 512/4Kn boundaries. open_work.title: Physical media, supported hosts and desktop qualification
open_work.finding: x86-64 simulated media and Qt evidence are extensive; physical unplug durability and additional host/desktop configurations are not fully qualified.
open_work.acceptance: Use one representative physical USB for write/readback, immediate unplug after joined READY and reconnect; one native 4Kn device if available; bounded hotplug/desktop-automount contention and cancellation/recovery. Build/run representative i686 and aarch64 Linux hosts in addition to x86-64. Exercise one X11 and one Wayland desktop, normal/enlarged DPI, RTL and keyboard/accessibility once. Record unavailable hardware honestly; no USB-model/distro-version matrix.
open_work.release_result: 32 substantive available desktop cases pass: native KDE Wayland and Qt xcb via KDE Xwayland at1x/2x, French/Arabic/Romanian live dialogs, keyboard/tab/close and large fonts. Standalone Xorg, physical input, additional complete hosts and unavailable media remain unqualified.

explicit_dispositions.title: Dormant ext4 format enum
explicit_dispositions.reason: FS_EXT4 has no enabled Windows UI cluster entry; format_ext.c falls back to ext3. Native ext4 persistence already exists. This is not a missing selectable ext4 data formatter.

explicit_dispositions.title: Unused AdvancedMode key
explicit_dispositions.reason: SETTING_ADVANCED_MODE has no exact runtime reader; ShowAdvancedDriveProperties and ShowAdvancedFormatOptions are the active, implemented panel settings.

explicit_dispositions.title: Dead DisableSecureBootNotice setting
explicit_dispositions.reason: Only generic notification code writes it; there is no active reader in this baseline. Do not invent an extra feature from the macro.

explicit_dispositions.title: Developer-only test/version helpers
explicit_dispositions.reason: Ctrl+T is compiled only for debug/TEST/ALPHA; IDC_TEST is hidden test machinery; -z forces Windows-version detection. These are not offered release media features.

explicit_dispositions.title: Session runtime-validation preference
explicit_dispositions.reason: Windows reading/writing EnableRuntimeValidation is commented out; native session-only behavior is correct.

explicit_dispositions.title: Windows autorun registry cleanup
explicit_dispositions.reason: Alt+X restores Windows NoDriveTypeAutorun state; native code never creates that registry/policy change. No Linux device action is required.

explicit_dispositions.title: Agreed host regional-settings behavior
explicit_dispositions.reason: Copy current Windows regional settings remains visible and disabled on Linux. Explicit source/user choices replace no other customization option; further host-setting inference is prohibited.

explicit_dispositions.title: Native package update ownership
explicit_dispositions.reason: CP68 documents why native multi-file packages update through distribution/package workflows rather than a Windows executable replacement. Actual release delivery remains Q03/Q04.

explicit_dispositions.title: Agreed FAT32 caption
explicit_dispositions.reason: Linux uses FAT32 at all sizes. This settles the name only; Alt+L/V observable formatting effects remain A02.

explicit_dispositions.title: Explicit DOS and initial language choices
explicit_dispositions.reason: FreeDOS starts at US/437 and language at English with explicit saved/menu choices, per user instructions. Do not add host locale/keyboard detection for parity.

explicit_dispositions.title: Autorun attribute claim corrected
explicit_dispositions.reason: Windows icon.c creates autorun.inf/icon as ordinary files, not hidden/system files. Kolibri-specific hidden/system loader attributes remain I19.

explicit_dispositions.title: Shared label normalization
explicit_dispositions.reason: format_policy.c NormalizeVolumeLabel is shared, including FAT non-ASCII replacement. Do not invent a Linux-only OEM-label gap.

explicit_dispositions.title: Native update consent bookkeeping
explicit_dispositions.reason: Windows CommCheck64/internal network state is represented by explicit native application/policy consent and separate timestamps. It is not another missing user setting.

explicit_dispositions.title: Windows autoplay group policy
explicit_dispositions.reason: DisableLGP controls Windows local group-policy mutations; native private mounts do not make those changes. Documented one-helper cleanup remains C15.

explicit_dispositions.title: Case-insensitive imported setting names
explicit_dispositions.reason: ApplicationStorage key lookup is case-insensitive and canonicalizes existing aliases; EnableVmdkDetection/EnableVMDKDetection and DisableRufusMBR capitalization are not missing imports.

One combined native route per build qualifies 5.10 FAT32, 6.03 NTFS and old families 3 FAT32/4 NTFS, exact EFI/COM32/checksum/link readback, Windows reparse metadata, one authorization and joined READY, with representative original Syslinux BIOS and embedded EFI/UEFI:NTFS handoffs. Existing unchanged helper/writer fault evidence reused.

batches.title: Legacy Windows, ReactOS and Kolibri ISO routes
batches.gate: Six focused component suites pass in normal and sanitizer builds: 1,897 substantive Qt cases, seven existing optional Microsoft-resource skips, plus 244 ISO/UDF extraction cases. All fourteen new legacy resource/protocol/source cases pass. One combined native route per build creates and reads back five jobs: legacy PE FAT16, unknown-version Windows FAT16 dual, ReactOS FAT32, legacy PE NTFS with EFI/UEFI:NTFS, and Kolibri FAT32. Exact MBR/PBR/source/prepared bytes, actual hidden/system FAT attributes, final NTFS dual layout/clean flags, one authorization and joined READY pass. Three representative firmware handoffs pass: native FAT16 EFI, original Syslinux/mboot ReactOS and Kolibri PBR. One full nine-suite Qt run plus focused normal/sanitizer repairs qualifies 2,214 substantive cases with 2 existing optional skips and no outstanding failures. The full run found twelve failures in one obsolete root-loader-refusal group (including one fixture startup failure); all twelve rows pass after its acceptance expectations are updated. Product sources remain unchanged after the full gate. The earlier focused UI group had two failures; one fixture expectation and the Kolibri phase contract were repaired, and all six B4 repair rows pass in normal and sanitizer builds. Existing unchanged helper faults and installed-Windows/customization evidence are reused.

batches.title: Sector and filesystem geometry
batches.gate: Grouped normal/sanitizer components qualify 13 unique suites and 778 substantive cases, no skips or outstanding failures. Initial checks found three obsolete/fault-interaction failures; focused repairs preserve the initial receipts and pass. One combined native route per build creates and independently reads back 21 ordinary Qt/helper jobs: seven formats at 512/512, 512/4096 and 4096/4096 across MBR/GPT/SFD, six stale-geometry refusals before authorization, one FAT32 full format, exact payloads where originally eligible and clean ext roots/superblocks, one authorization per job and joined READY. A representative native FAT32 EFI handoff passes. Sparse component fixtures cover capacity/cluster/provider boundaries including the actual maximum native 4-KiB UDF volume. The single full nine-suite Qt run plus a focused normal/sanitizer native-ioctl fixture and cluster-choice repairs qualifies 2,215 substantive cases with 2 existing optional skips and zero outstanding failures. The full run exposed an obsolete ioctl fixture that omitted BLKPBSZGET and one cluster-choice assertion expecting four options before 64 KiB was restored; all 53 cases in the affected device suite and the single cluster row pass after repair. Prior unchanged writer faults and installed-Windows/customization evidence are reused.

completed_work.title: Cache, priority, USB diagnostics and log keyboard action
completed_work.acceptance: Provide all three actions with original session/saved behavior and idle/active guards. Priority must affect actual workers through a documented native scheduling mapping; diagnostics must affect enumeration/logging. Delete only owned downloaded resources, invalidate retained cache selections and preserve sources, settings and logs. Match visible-log Ctrl+A routing without stealing ordinary text selection when the log is closed.
completed_work.audit_finding: Alt+D, Alt plus/minus and Alt+. have no native actions; DefaultThreadPriority and EnableUsbDebug are not consumed. Windows Ctrl+A selects a visible log even when another window owns focus; native standard editor selection is focus-local.

completed_work.acceptance: Offer and persist an explicit light/dark override with coherent restart/recreation behavior, readable controls and unchanged active-job completion.
completed_work.audit_finding: The desktop theme is used, but the saved Ctrl+Alt+D user override is absent.

completed_work.title: Advanced application update diagnostics and force mode
completed_work.acceptance: Implement the explicit advanced force mode and meaningful verbose diagnostics for the native release service; retain consent, channel, origin and architecture checks. Invalid dates in ordinary mode must still preserve the last successful timestamp.
completed_work.audit_finding: Ordinary Alt+Y exists. Ctrl+Alt+Y timestamp-ignore force mode and the verbose update setting have no native counterpart.
completed_work.native_difference: Windows Ctrl+Alt+Y bypasses Authenticode executable-signature timestamps, not HTTP Date. Native updates delegate package verification; both force shortcuts retain strict HTTP dates/TLS and log the Windows-specific boundary. Verbose levels 0/1/2 are preserved.

completed_work.title: Raw optical disc capture
completed_work.acceptance: Discover readable optical media, choose the original applicable disc source, save exact device bytes transactionally, support progress/cancel/read failures and release all read handles before successful completion. Reuse capture destination publication; do not mount or rewrite the source.
completed_work.audit_finding: USB filesystem-to-UDF ISO export is delivered; Alt+O raw optical media capture is a distinct missing source workflow.

completed_work.title: USB port reset and GPT ESP type toggle

completed_work.audit_finding: Alt+C device port cycling and Alt+P ESP-to-data/original-type restoration have no native command path.

completed_work.title: Configured device exclusion tables

completed_work.audit_finding: Eight IgnoreUsb VID/PID slots and eight IgnoreDisk decorated-GUID slots are not read natively.

Reuse the writer; qualify one route per distinct native class, not per virtual-disk vendor.

completed_work.title: Mounted source and caller-home backing resolution
completed_work.acceptance: Resolve Btrfs member disks, file-backed loop and stacked block relationships for source/home protection and automatic unmount. Support positively resolvable overlay/FUSE backing and positively identified nonlocal sources; retain explicit refusal for opaque unresolved backing. Keep every parent/container/supplementary source protected, with one helper and no prewrite changes on refusal.
completed_work.audit_finding: Direct block/fuseblk and memory sources work. The shared source/home check refuses loop-backed and unresolved anonymous mounts; CP65 application backing resolution has broader support that is not reused here.

completed_work.title: Drive-locking override
completed_work.acceptance: Implement a meaningful explicit native opt-out retaining identity, source protection and sync/cleanup, or document and demonstrate the concrete Linux requirement preventing it. An inert toggle or generic safety preference does not close this row; any unavoidable divergence must satisfy AGENTS.md.
completed_work.audit_finding: Windows exposes a session opt-out of physical-drive locking; the native helper requires an exclusive claim.

completed_work.title: Windows-specific virtual-disk parent locators
completed_work.acceptance: Determine the exact Windows desktop-supported alternate locator/linkage cases. Provide explicit native parent/path mapping or relocation input for original-supported nonportable paths, validating parent IDs, geometry and timestamps and retaining every source before authorization. Do not infer Windows drive letters from Linux paths or rewrite the source container. Record any format-defined locator case the desktop API itself does not accept.
completed_work.audit_finding: Relative VHD/VHDX chains and immutable log replay are delivered. Drive/UNC-only locator resolution and parent_linkage2 are explicitly unsupported.

completed_work.title: Source-selected EFI architectures
completed_work.acceptance: Admit and validate original-eligible ia32, x64, arm, aa64, ia64, riscv64, loongarch64 and ebc source fallback applications with correct machine/format checks and source names. Keep selection based on source, not host. Reuse existing generic UEFI:NTFS/runtime resources; preserve IA64/EBC without inventing missing Windows validator binaries. Windows-specific repair/customization must retain its actual architecture eligibility.
completed_work.audit_finding: Ordinary ISO creation preflights only bootx64.efi/PE32+. The shared scanner recognizes eight EFI architecture names.

completed_work.title: Embedded FAT EFI extraction and broken-link repair
completed_work.acceptance: Extract the original eligible embedded EFI tree and replace a proven broken fallback link as Windows does. Validate paths, machine type and retained source before authorization, include embedded EFI binaries in security analysis and final checksum/space planning, and preserve regular source fallback precedence.
completed_work.audit_finding: Embedded EFI FAT inspection exists, but extraction/fallback repair and security enumeration of those files are not integrated into the native ISO write path.

completed_work.title: ISO symbolic links and nonregular-entry compatibility
completed_work.acceptance: Reproduce resolved file/directory links as Windows-compatible NTFS reparse links; implement FAT syslinux-to-isolinux materialization, /firmware target duplication and original literal-target/skip rules. Match Windows UDF entry-as-file behavior for its supported link cases. Resolve only within the retained image/output tree; never follow source-controlled links into the host. Include checksum and companion configuration updates.
completed_work.audit_finding: The native extractor rejects Rock Ridge symlinks and UDF nonregular entries that Windows processes.

completed_work.title: Image-matched Syslinux versions and obsolete modules
completed_work.acceptance: Support Windows-accepted Syslinux major families 3/4/5/6 by their actual version/resource contract, full suffix then original base fallback. Implement signed/cache/download/cancel handling for selected companion pairs and the two obsolete COM32 modules with original thresholds. Reject unknown incompatible payloads explicitly; avoid a per-distribution or every-release test matrix.
completed_work.audit_finding: The ISO installer is pinned to the qualified 6.04-pre1 resources. Windows selects source-matched ldlinux.sys/bss and can replace old menu.c32/vesamenu.c32.

completed_work.title: Slax relocation and missing-directory ISO recovery
completed_work.acceptance: Move /slax/boot/EFI to /EFI only under original absence/precedence rules, retain accompanying Syslinux config selection, and create missing safe parents for the exact Windows-supported mastering fault. Prove generated positive/refusal cases and final checksum updates; never accept traversal, absolute paths or conflicting aliases.
completed_work.audit_finding: The native ISO copy path lacks the original Slax EFI relocation and recovery when an ISO omits parent-directory entries.

completed_work.title: Syslinux v4 host portability
completed_work.acceptance: Port the original v4 accessor/install path to alignment-safe endian-correct native C on aarch64 while preserving x86 bytes. Keep upstream provenance, provider build/install registration and representative installer/readback checks. This is a host-tool gap, separate from image EFI architecture.
completed_work.audit_finding: The native Syslinux 4.07 build explicitly stops on non-x86 hosts because its unmodified non-x86 accessors are unsuitable.

completed_work.title: Secure Boot issuer lookup outside embedded certificates
completed_work.acceptance: Add bounded native cached/system issuer lookup with deterministic embedded-versus-cache precedence and the original signer fallback. Preserve issuer metadata classification rather than treating successful chain construction as publisher authentication. No live AIA/network fetch is required; cover missing, ambiguous and unavailable issuers.
completed_work.audit_finding: Windows cache-only chain lookup may find an immediate issuer outside the signed image. Native lookup currently uses the embedded certificate collection only.

completed_work.title: Windows and legacy FAT16 boot routes
completed_work.acceptance: Reproduce Windows-eligible FAT16 BIOS/dual and older UEFI source paths using exact original PBR/loader expectations. Cover normalized Windows 7/8/8.1/10/11 and legacy i386/amd64/minint only where Windows actually offers them. Verify copied bytes, generated loader handoff and source restrictions; do not schedule installed-Windows/customization tests.
completed_work.audit_finding: Native Windows BIOS/dual admits FAT32 or NTFS; older UEFI explicitly refuses FAT16, and legacy WinPE FAT16 remains gated.

completed_work.title: Older BOOTMGR, PE and mixed-loader dispatch
completed_work.acceptance: Handle the finite original source classes: older normalized-unknown BOOTMGR installers (including Vista), BOOTMGR/WIM PE without an install archive, and i386/amd64/minint with the additional BOOTMGR/EFI/install-archive or loader combinations selected by original GetBootInstallType/GetSecondaryBootType. Preserve existing SIF encodings, loader ownership and NTFS repair requirements; compare representative dispatch/bytes without a per-release OS-install matrix.
completed_work.audit_finding: The known-installer predicate restricts releases to 7/8/8.1/10/11. Existing WinPE preparation works for its qualified families but rejects BOOTMGR-EFI/install-archive mixtures and other original dispatch cases.
completed_work.native_difference: Original Windows invokes Fmifs CheckDisk after NTFS ISO creation. Native Linux retains the qualified PBR-before-mount, checked writes, sync and private unmount, with independent clean-volume/readback and existing boot evidence. This is not Windows CheckDisk; original Windows API and installed WinPE/AIK execution remain unqualified under the retained Q02 scope. No alternate provider or arbitrary-corruption repair is attempted.

completed_work.title: ReactOS and KolibriOS ISO creation
completed_work.acceptance: Deliver both original ISO dispatch routes: ReactOS loader/Syslinux selection and freeldr/setupldr files; Kolibri FAT32/PBR with its root MTLD_F32 loader and actual hidden/system attributes. Retain original FAT16 refusal where applicable and native authorization/sync/cleanup/boot handoff.
completed_work.audit_finding: Standalone ReactOS is delivered. ReactOS ISO and KolibriOS ISO are explicitly refused by ordinary native creation.

completed_work.title: Logical 4-KiB formatting geometry
completed_work.acceptance: Carry real logical/physical sector geometry through discovery, requests, plans, all eligible filesystem providers, boot records and readback. Qualify 512/512e and 4096 logical-byte cases at actual policy boundaries on MBR/GPT/SFD; preserve native raw support and explicit filesystem/boot limits.
completed_work.audit_finding: Raw writing already accepts its native sector range. Formatting/layout/provider options are hard-coded to 512 logical bytes and reject 4Kn.
completed_work.native_difference: Original Windows warns before trying non-512 bootable media; its SBR code has an explicit 4K TODO. Native original BIOS/DOS/Syslinux/SBR and bundled UEFI:NTFS paths retain their executable 512-byte contract and refuse other logical sectors before writes. Native UEFI FAT/data formatting qualifies 4Kn. Small ext volumes use blocks at least as large as the real logical sector for a mountable Linux filesystem.

completed_work.title: UDF block size and volume geometry
completed_work.acceptance: Choose and verify 512/1024/2048/4096 UDF logical blocks where allowed by real device/provider geometry; separate UDF block size from device sector size. Cover transitions and bounded descriptor/anchor arithmetic. Establish the actual maximum supported by the Windows formatter/provider, rather than claiming all volumes under its 256-TiB UI cap necessarily format.
completed_work.audit_finding: The native UDF writer and verifier use 512-byte blocks and a 32-bit block-count limit, restricting volumes to approximately 2 TiB.
completed_work.native_difference: Microsoft documents 2^32 UDF blocks; actual Windows formatter execution at that boundary remains unqualified under Q02. Rufus passes provider-default allocation rather than proving its 256-TiB UI cap. Native mkudffs requires UDF blocks equal device logical sectors and supports UINT32_MAX blocks; excess capacity is refused before its silent truncation. Exact native 2/4/8/16-TiB-minus-one-block boundaries are established and tested.

completed_work.title: Forced FAT32 formatter and Windows VDS backend controls
completed_work.acceptance: Compare original observable cluster, quick-format, full-format and eligibility effects of ForceLargeFat32Formatting and UseVds against the native path. Implement missing effects or document a tested coherent single-provider equivalent. Do not reproduce Windows API selection with a no-op control.
completed_work.audit_finding: Linux already uses one native FAT32 formatter at every size and the agreed FAT32 label. Separate Windows FormatEx/large-FAT/VDS switches are absent.
completed_work.native_difference: One native FAT32 provider implements original cluster eligibility including 64 KiB, checked quick/full formats and labels. Full formats remain offered through 32 GiB, while Windows forcing its large provider disables this even below that boundary. Native metadata placement may differ by provider. Windows API/backend toggles are not exposed as no-ops. ReFS remains I15/B7.

completed_work.title: Distribution packages and dependency delivery
completed_work.acceptance: Deliver/inspect one Debian-family package and one RPM-family package alongside existing Arch/generic delivery. Check fresh install, helper/polkit/resource paths, required provider/runtime versions, upgrade and removal on one representative environment each. Record supported host/package combinations, rather than promising every distribution.
completed_work.audit_finding: Arch/CachyOS and generic archive packages are delivered; Debian/RPM dependency/install qualification remains separate from media algorithms.
completed_work.qualification_limits: Debian13/Fedora44 x86-64 native builds and rootless-container fresh install, same-payload lower-package-release upgrade and removal. Arch source recipe clean-built with native Arch dependencies. No prior public distro application-version migration, physical USB or polkit-agent UI claimed. AUR submission will be performed manually by the user.
